recommendation: Keep the audit commit and leave the current Group documentation as-is. FHIR-I or the responsible editor should first decide where core-owned Application Feature Framework FeatureDefinitions live, then add a canonical Group membership-filter support feature and examples/assertions in the appropriate FHIR-core or HL7/capstmt source.
issue_request: FHIR-50592 was an Applied/Persuasive FHIR-core Group issue asking how servers should declare support for enumerated-only or characteristic Group membership filters. The resolution says this can be documented non-computably in CapabilityStatement.rest.resource.documentation markdown and that core should define a corresponding Application Feature Framework feature.
initial_application: Commit 73d80b15379961e418e9cae1cd24a5b9649f5757 added the CapabilityStatement.rest.resource.documentation sentence to source/group/group-notes.xml. The Group resource is active in source/fhir.ini, so that narrative is in build scope. No FHIR-core source artifact defining a computable Group-filter feature was found.
additional_context: FHIR-I WGM minutes from May 2025 record that FHIR-50592 could be represented non-computably through CapabilityStatement documentation or computably through the Application Feature Framework, then note the final proposal would likely be partially applied until a place exists to define core features. The current HL7/capstmt Application Feature Framework IG says it only defines FeatureSupport, and GitHub code search found no FHIR-50592 or Group FeatureDefinition there.
reconciliation: Published an empty human-review audit commit. No source change was made because the safe core documentation edit already exists, while adding an invented FeatureDefinition or speculative prose would not safely satisfy the computable feature clause.
